I don't have any notes on Psalm 131 to give you yet. The research stopped before I could read a single source.

My first attempt to download the commentary pages hit an error in my own code. I then ran out of the web tool calls allowed for this turn, so I couldn't retry. Your rule is to report only what the pages actually say, so I won't fill in notes from memory.

**Pages I'll read next time:**
- enduringword.com/bible-commentary/psalm-131/
- biblehub.com, the Psalm 131 pages for Ellicott, Gill and the Pulpit Commentary
- preceptaustin.org, Psalm 131 commentary
- netbible.org, the translator's notes on Psalm 131 (for modern scholarship)
- A search across the other sites you listed for:
  - views from each Protestant tradition (Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*, Wesley's notes, Ligonier, the Lutheran sites and others)
  - Catholic and Orthodox readings (newadvent.org, which has Augustine's sermon on this psalm, plus catholic.com and oca.org)
  - any discussion of popular modern teaching

**What the notes will include:**
- Verse-by-verse notes ("v. 1: …"), with a URL after every point.
- Disagreements between traditions, but only where the sources actually show them.
- Nothing I couldn't find.

If you reply "go ahead," I'll run the research properly and write the notes.
